terrace_management_practices.title: Dry-Stone Riser and Bund Reinforcement
terrace_management_practices.purpose: Prevent terrace collapse, soil wash-off during sudden snowmelt or monsoon downpours, and retain moisture.
instructions: Inspect the terrace edge (riser) after winter freeze-thaw cycles for bulging or loose stones.
Re-stack stones with a slight inward batter (slope leaning into the hill terrace) of 1:5.
Pack small gravel directly behind the stone wall to allow seepage of excess water without carrying precious topsoil.
Establish vegetative bund cover using deep-rooted perennial grasses or broad bean border rows.
terrace_management_practices.source_reference: ICAR-VPKAS Almora Res. Bull. 38: Soil and Water Conservation on Himalayan Agricultural Terraces

terrace_management_practices.title: Raised Cold-Terrace Planting Beds (15-20 cm)
terrace_management_practices.purpose: Warm soil 3-5°C faster in spring, avoid waterlogging in clay or poorly drained soils, and improve root aeration.
instructions: Mark 1-meter wide planting beds running along the contour of the terrace (never perpendicular to slope).
Dig shallow pathways (30 cm wide) between beds and mound topsoil onto the bed to create a 15-20 cm raised platform.
Incorporate 4-5 kg/m² well-rotted farmyard manure (FYM) or mature compost into the upper 10 cm.
Crown the center of the bed slightly so excess rainfall sheds smoothly into the perimeter drainage furrows.
terrace_management_practices.source_reference: GBPUAT Hill Agriculture Extension Manual & ICAR-VPKAS

terrace_management_practices.title: Thermal Micro-Cloche and Organic Straw Mulching
terrace_management_practices.purpose: Protect emerging seedlings from lethal -2°C to -6°C nocturnal radiation frosts and conserve moisture.
tools_materials: Dry mountain grass or wheat/barley straw
UV-stabilized clear poly-sheet or agrifleece (30-50 GSM)
instructions: After direct sowing or transplanting, spread a 5-7 cm layer of dry straw between plant rows, keeping mulch 2 cm away from stems.
Bend flexible bamboo arches every 1.2 meters over the terrace bed.
Drape lightweight agrifleece or polythene over arches before sunset when frost is forecasted.
Ventilate or roll up covers during sunny midday hours to prevent heat stress and humidity spikes.
terrace_management_practices.source_reference: SKUAST-K & KVK Leh Bulletin on Protected Mountain Agriculture

terrace_management_practices.title: Terrace Windbreak and Solar Heat Retention
terrace_management_practices.purpose: Buffer against desiccating cold Himalayan winds and maximize thermal energy capture on north/west terraces.
instructions: Erect a 1.2m semi-permeable woven brushwood screen on the terrace edge facing prevailing mountain winds (usually NW/N).
Place dark river cobbles or slate stones along northern bed borders: they absorb daytime solar radiation and re-radiate warmth during cold nights.
Avoid solid impermeable walls which create damaging wind eddies over delicate crops.
terrace_management_practices.source_reference: Dr. Y.S. Parmar UHF Solan Extension Guide

terrace_management_practices.title: Irrigation Water Pre-Warming Basin
terrace_management_practices.purpose: Prevent root temperature shock caused by icy glacial snowmelt or mountain stream water (often 3-6°C).
tools_materials: Dark 200L drum or shallow earthen pit lined with black plastic
instructions: Fill the holding basin or dark drum with stream/spring water in the early morning.
Allow sun to warm water to ambient temperature (12-18°C) before applying to root zones in late morning (10 AM - 12 PM).
Never irrigate in the late evening, as wet foliage will freeze solid during nocturnal frost events.
